newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland policewoman shot but not seriously hurt.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland policewoman shot but not seriously hurt.

text.p: A Northern Ireland policewoman received facial injuries on Sunday night when a gunman fired on a police vehicle in a wave of Catholic anger over the holding of an Orange Order parade in Portadown.
She was part of a patrol sitting in a vehicle in the town of Coalisland north of Portadown when a gunman emerged and fired what was thought to be a shotgun.
The policewoman was injured in the face but her wounds were not life-threatening, police said.
Further details were not immediately available but Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas or a splinter faction fighting British rule of Northern Ireland were under suspicion, security sources said.
A music festival was being held in the town at the time and the patrol was thought to be part of a crowd control team.
It was the second shooting incident following the parade, which was held over the objections of Catholic Irish nationalists living along the Garvaghy Road of Portadown.
Earlier a masked gunman emerged from a Belfast side street in a Catholic area and fired five shots at a police vehicle without causing injury. He escaped into a side street.
Both incidents highlighted violent Catholic opposition to the holding of the parade by the Protestant order against the wishes of local pro-Irish residents.
Police said several cars were hijacked and set ablaze by youths as part of protests which hit Catholic areas of Belfast and the province's second city, Londonderry.
Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA, held two major rallies in the cities on Sunday night which were addressed by the party's leaders, Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness.
